comments.body:
I think yes, this is a good direction, with one important boundary: the static site should not call the GitHub workflow API directly with any repo credential. The button should either route through an authenticated Sepo/server endpoint, or open a GitHub/manual dispatch surface for users who already have permission.

Repo fit looks good:

- Citation behavior already lives in [`quartz/plugins/local/literature-citations/index.js`](https://github.com/self-evolving/literature-template/blob/main/quartz/plugins/local/literature-citations/index.js#L541-L566).
- Missing paper notes already render a bibliography popover instead of an internal paper link at [`index.js#L621-L655`](https://github.com/self-evolving/literature-template/blob/main/quartz/plugins/local/literature-citations/index.js#L621-L655).
- The add-paper workflow already accepts `paper`, `additional_request`, and `base_branch` via `workflow_dispatch` in [`agent-add-paper.yml#L4-L19`](https://github.com/self-evolving/literature-template/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-add-paper.yml#L4-L19), then creates a PR at [`agent-add-paper.yml#L225-L237`](https://github.com/self-evolving/literature-template/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-add-paper.yml#L225-L237).

Suggested implementation shape:

1. Add the button only in the missing-paper citation popover, where we have a BibTeX entry but no matching `content/papers/<citekey>.md`.
2. Pass a high-quality payload: preferably the BibTeX entry, plus `additional_request` like `Add paper note for @citekey cited from <current page>`.
3. Dispatch through a backend/authenticated route, not from browser JS with a token.
4. Show a clear pending/submitted state and avoid duplicate clicks for the same citekey.
5. After dispatch, rely on `agent-add-paper.yml` to create the branch, validate, and open the PR.

So: yes on the UX and workflow model. The main design decision is the auth boundary for dispatching the workflow.
